page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.48xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is equipped with 192 vCPUs and 96 physical cores utilizing Intel Xeon 8559C processors running at a sustained clock speed of 3.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The underlying hardware incorporates Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction set extensions. System memory consists of 1536 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 6 GHz, yielding an allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided via 120,000 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD capacity, and network connectivity supports a baseline throughput of 200 Gbps.

Benchmark testing highlights strong multi-core computational efficiency and memory throughput. The instance recorded a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 169940.36 and a PassMark CPU score of 131650.09, both residing in the top tier of evaluated hardware. Uncached memory bandwidth reached 571.21 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 240.52 GB/sec for write operations. Data handling capabilities demonstrated high operational scaling, achieving 203.2 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 214.44 GB/sec.

The primary operational advantage of the i7ie.48xlarge rests in its extreme density of bundled NVMe storage and DDR5 memory per socket, offering optimal cost efficiency for large-scale data engines without incurring network storage overhead. A notable tradeoff is its single-core performance, which registers in the average tier with a stress-ng score of 2112.78, confirming that performance relies heavily on multi-threaded parallel execution. Lacking dedicated GPU hardware, machine learning acceleration is restricted to CPU-based execution. The instance is suited for high-throughput relational databases, distributed key-value stores, real-time analytics, and data-intensive ETL processing.
description: Amazon Web Services i7ie.48xlarge is a high-density storage-optimized server engineered around 192 vCPUs from Intel Xeon 8559C processors at 3.2 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it integrates 1536 GB of DDR5 RAM and 120,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage with a 200 Gbps network interface. Multi-threaded benchmark results fall into the top tier, evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 169940.36 and Redis SET throughput of 203.2 million operations per second. Hardware capabilities include AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets, supporting vectorized computation and CPU-based LLM inference. While single-threaded processing is moderate, the system delivers high uncached memory bandwidth and low-latency disk I/O. This resource configuration is designed for enterprise relational databases, large in-memory key-value caches, and distributed data analytics workloads.
